bull.b: Lower debt reduces fixed financial obligations and may provide more flexibility as Tempest funds clinical development. This improvement is meaningful for a clinical-stage company, although the benefit is partly offset by the recent deterioration in equity.

The collaboration broadens Tempest’s development platform into an emerging in vivo CAR-T area and could add a Phase 1 multiple myeloma program plus autoimmune applications. If the option is exercised, the portfolio may strengthen long-term pipeline depth.

A committed equity facility gives Tempest discretion to access capital over time rather than relying only on a single financing event. That flexibility can support ongoing corporate and development needs, though future share issuance may dilute existing holders.

bear.b: Tempest has no commercial revenue to offset research and development spending, leaving financial performance dependent on future clinical progress, partnering, or commercialization. Persistent losses limit internal funding capacity and make a near-term path to profitability uncertain.

Continued cash outflows require recurring access to external financing while negative equity reduces balance-sheet flexibility. Together, these conditions can constrain investment in the pipeline and increase the company’s dependence on equity or other funding sources.

The minimum-bid deficiency creates a continuing listing requirement that management must address while advancing the business. Failure to regain compliance could lead to delisting proceedings, potentially complicating financing access and reducing institutional participation.
